YouTube title seed: How Does a Streetlight Know It's Night?
YouTube description seed: That little dome on top of some lights is making a decision every evening. What did you think it was? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: A small light sensor decides when the lamp turns on.
The later surprise: It has a short delay so passing headlights cannot fool it.
The very first frame shows a home dusk-to-dawn light flicking on in bright daylight, its small round sensor visible on top, no hand in frame. Already moving in the first frame; do not reveal the mechanism in the opening.
What changes inside each 6s clip:
Scene 1 (contradiction, 0-6s): Opening: the lamp flicks on in daylight with no hand in frame. About 2s in, framing moves closer to the small sensor on top. About 4s in, a hand enters and lifts a cap off the sensor, revealing that it had been covered.
Scene 2 (clue, 6-12s): Mechanism starts about 5s in. The cap lifts off and the lamp turns off after a short delay (wait trimmed); about 2-3s later, a macro of the sensor lens against the sky; then a timelapse of the sky dimming.
Scene 3 (mechanism, 12-18s): A real photocell unit opened on a workbench, its sensor and relay visible as physical parts (no animation or cutaway); about 2s in, a flashlight shines on it and a lamp stays off; about 4s in, a hand shades it and the lamp clicks on.
Scene 4 (second_reveal, 18-24s): The dusk-to-dawn light at evening; about 2s in, car headlights sweep across it; about 4s in, the lamp stays steady, unfooled.
Scene 5 (payoff, 24-30s): A street at dusk with lamps coming on; about 3s in, return to the exact opening: the same home light flicking on in daylight with its sensor visible on top and no hand in frame, same framing as scene 1's first frame, so it loops.
Fact boundaries: Not every streetlight has its own photocell; some use timers, central controls, or one photocell for a whole circuit. Film the cover demo on a home or garden dusk-to-dawn light, not a public streetlight; never climb poles or tamper with city equipment. The switch is not instant; covering can take up to about 30-60 seconds.

facts.statement: Many streetlights use a photocell, a light sensor that switches the lamp on when daylight falls below a set level and off again at dawn.
In daylight the sensor keeps a relay holding the lamp off; in the dark the relay lets power through and the lamp turns on.
Covering a dusk-to-dawn light's photocell turns the light on after a short delay, and the delay stops brief light changes from fooling it.
